correctness.rationale: For every nondegenerate axis-reflection-symmetric convex meridian L and R exceeding its radial semiextent, classify random affine-plane sections of the solid of revolution by annulus, one disk, and two disks. Fibers over azimuth have interval domain and strictly monotone support endpoints, yielding exact offset measures 2(H-Rsinθ)_+ and 2(Rsinθ-H)_+ for annulus and two-disk sections. Haar integration gives all three probabilities, including Euler-characteristic mean. For a C² positive-curvature meridian, differentiating the all-radii annulus profile gives minus the strictly monotone angular primitive F(θ_R), recovers H(θ)/sinθ pointwise, and thereby uniquely reconstructs L. The standalone numerical checker agrees in 797 azimuth cases, 450,000 random-plane trials and 15 inversion tests; these tests corroborate rather than replace the analytic arguments.

value.rationale: A toroidal solid naturally has nonconvex planar cuts with nontrivial topology; its three-type topological law gives a complete exact stereological invariant for every convex symmetric meridian. Recovering the entire positively curved meridian from this topological law across revolution radii is a substantive inverse-geometric theorem, strictly stronger than calculating probabilities for a circular torus. The formula also establishes a universal Euler-characteristic profile and a nontrivial topology-difference identity.
